hero.lead: A nation of 18.1 million with farmland across half its land and a €5.4 billion recovery and resilience plan, with public debt of 44.7% of GDP.

capital.heading: Engineered against the sea, and every income secured.

register.name: New 20-year Dutch State Loan, DSL 2048
register.detail: Dutch State Treasury Agency · Dutch Direct Auction 29 September 2026 · coupon 3.75% · matures 15 January 2048 · issuance yield 3.990%
register.note: €24.03 billion in bids in the order book
register.text: A new 20-year bond of the Dutch State, sold by Dutch Direct Auction at an annual coupon of 3.75%. It funds the central government budget as a whole, which carries the seven standards; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of them.

register.name: Five-year Social Bond, NWB Bank
register.detail: NWB Bank · issued 8 September 2026 · coupon 3.250% · matures 15 October 2031 · reoffer yield 3.355%, mid-swaps +9bps
register.note: Proceeds fully allocated to loans for Dutch social housing associations
register.text: A social bond of NWB Bank, which lends to the Dutch public sector, whose proceeds fund loans to social housing associations for affordable and environmentally sustainable rental housing for lower-income households. It serves the shelter standard and the households on the lowest incomes.

register.name: Seven-year Water Bond, NWB Bank
register.detail: NWB Bank · priced 28 May 2026 · coupon 3.0% · matures 3 June 2033 · reoffer yield 3.083%, mid-swaps +19bps
register.note: Proceeds go to the Dutch water authorities, for flood protection, water management and water quality
register.text: A green bond of NWB Bank whose proceeds are lent to the Dutch water authorities, whose tasks are flood protection, water management and water quality. It serves the water standard and keeps homes and farmland safe from flooding.

register.name: Green Dutch State Loans
register.detail: Dutch State Treasury Agency · outstanding at 31 December 2025 · €2.055 billion raised in the Green DSL 2044 by tap auction in 2025 · Green Bond Report 2025 published 28 May 2026
register.note: Allocated to renewable energy, energy efficiency, sustainable transport, and climate adaptation and sustainable water management
register.text: The green bonds of the Dutch State, whose proceeds are allocated to climate-related expenditure and reported on each year. They finance renewable energy, energy efficiency and water management, serving the energy, water and shelter standards.

register.name: New 10-year Dutch State Loan, DSL 2036
register.detail: Dutch State Treasury Agency · Dutch Direct Auction 3 March 2026 · coupon 2.75% · matures 15 July 2036 · issuance yield 2.995%
register.note: €24.1 billion in bids in the order book
register.text: A new 10-year bond of the Dutch State at an annual coupon of 2.75%, sold by Dutch Direct Auction. It funds the central government budget as a whole, which carries the seven standards; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of them.

register.name: New 5-year Dutch State Loan, DSL 2031
register.detail: Dutch State Treasury Agency · auction 13 January 2026 · coupon 2.50% · matures 15 January 2031 · average yield 2.526%
register.note: Auctioned through the screens of MTS Netherlands; settled 15 January 2026
register.text: A new five-year bond of the Dutch State at an annual coupon of 2.50%, sold by auction. It funds the central government budget as a whole, which carries the seven standards; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of them.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission and Council of the EU · amended plan approved 20 January 2026 · in grants · fourth payment request of €661 million assessed positively 7 September 2026
register.note: The plan includes over 820,000 energy-saving upgrades for homes
register.text: EU grants under the Recovery and Resilience Facility for agreed reforms and investments, among them energy-saving upgrades for homes, help for jobless people to find work, up- and reskilling, a more resilient public health system and the digitalisation of education. It serves the energy, shelter, livelihood, health and education standards.

register.name: Grid reinforcement, Enexis
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 27 July 2026 · about 2,800 km of medium-voltage and 1,800 km of low-voltage cable · Groningen, Drenthe, Overijssel, Noord-Brabant and Limburg
register.note: Enexis serves 3 million households and businesses
register.text: An EIB financing facility for Enexis, a regional grid operator, to reinforce and expand the electricity network as demand for new connections grows. It serves the energy standard for households and businesses in five provinces.

register.name: Energy-efficiency loans, Nationaal Warmtefonds
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 20 July 2026 · total cost about €200 million · loans to households and homeowners’ associations
register.note: Meets demand from lower-income segments and homeowners’ associations
register.text: EIB financing for the Nationaal Warmtefonds, which lends to individual households and homeowners’ associations for energy-efficient renovation of their homes, including households on lower incomes. It serves the energy and shelter standards.

register.name: Drinking water network, PWN
register.detail: European Investment Bank · 10 July 2026 · InvestEU · PWN investment programme 2026–2029 · about 750 km of pipelines renewed, renovated or newly installed
register.note: About 35,000 new connections; PWN supplies more than 800,000 households, businesses and public institutions in North Holland
register.text: An EIB loan to PWN, the drinking water company of North Holland, to modernise, expand and future-proof its distribution network, with new pipelines, service connections and water meters. It serves the water standard for one of the most densely populated provinces.

register.name: OLVG hospital redevelopment, Amsterdam
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 27 March 2026 · first phase to 2031 · with partner banks and the Waarborgfonds voor de Zorgsector
register.note: OLVG will redevelop its West site in four main phases by 2047
register.text: An EIB loan for the first phase of the redevelopment of OLVG, Amsterdam’s city hospital, with new energy-efficient buildings and digital care that reaches patients at home. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Lending to healthcare and educational institutions, BNG Bank
register.detail: European Investment Bank · lending agreement 8 June 2023 · on-lent by BNG Bank on favourable terms
register.note: Can generate €600 million in loans, as the EIB typically finances up to 50% of a project
register.text: An EIB loan to BNG Bank, on-lent on favourable terms to Dutch public sector entities, mainly healthcare and educational institutions. It serves the health and education standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: Herenboeren
items.text: A cooperative model, founded by Ashoka Fellow Geert van der Veer, in which about 200 households co-own a nature-driven farm, hire a farmer and share its seasonal harvest, with 22 farms in operation and almost 10,000 households engaged.

items.name: Phood Farm
items.text: An aquaponic care farm and community farm in the south-east of Eindhoven that grows vegetables indoors and outdoors, sells them directly to consumers and businesses, and gives work and daytime activities to young people facing obstacles to work, such as autism, ADHD or burnout.

items.name: Energie van Ons
items.text: A national cooperative energy supplier, formed in July 2026 by the merger of Energie VanOns and om | nieuwe energie, that supplies locally generated, 100% renewable energy without a profit motive and brings together more than 250 local energy cooperatives.

items.name: Buurtzorg
items.text: A nurse-led home-care organisation founded in 2006 whose small, self-managing neighbourhood teams grew in its first ten years to more than 10,000 nurses in 850 teams in towns and villages across the Netherlands.

items.name: Prins Heerlijk
items.text: Training centres with a lunch café, a restaurant and a healthcare centre where young people aged 16 to 27 with learning difficulties learn to work in catering, retail or healthcare, almost 400 of them in 2023, with some 75 vocational diplomas and 110 paid jobs each year.

items.name: Brownies&downieS
items.text: A social franchise of cafés, part of the caterer Albron since 2022, where colleagues at a distance from the labour market work alongside other staff, listed at 58 locations across the Netherlands in its autumn 2025 menu.

items.name: Oscar Circulair
items.text: A waste-collection enterprise in Amsterdam and Rotterdam that collects and sorts the waste of local businesses through entrepreneurs’ collectives and employs “Oscars”, people from varied backgrounds, some in vulnerable positions on the job market, 14 of whom joined in 2023.
